# TinyWow Now - full tool guide

Last updated: 2026-11-23

## Merge PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/merge-pdf
Merge PDF joins two or more PDF files into one document, in the order you choose. It runs in your browser, so your files stay on your device, and the merged PDF keeps selectable text and original image quality.

How to use:
1. Drag in two or more PDF files, or click Choose files.
2. Move the files up or down until they sit in the order you want.
3. Click Merge PDF, then download merged.pdf.

Limits:
- The tool cannot merge password-protected PDFs. Remove the password first, and the tool names the protected file.
- Your device memory sets the practical limit. A few dozen normal documents merge without trouble on most computers.
- The tool joins whole files. It does not reorder single pages inside a file.

Q: How many PDF files can I merge at once?
A: You can merge as many files as your device memory allows. A few dozen normal documents merge without trouble on most computers.

Q: Does merging reduce quality?
A: No. The tool copies pages as they are, so text stays selectable and images keep their original quality.

Q: Can I change the order after I add the files?
A: Yes. Use the up and down arrows next to each file. The merged pages follow the order of the list.

Q: Why does the tool refuse one of my files?
A: The file is probably password protected or damaged. Remove the password in the app that created the file, then try again.

---

## Split PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/split-pdf
Split PDF separates one PDF into single pages, or extracts the pages you choose, such as 1-3, 5, 8-10, into a new PDF. It runs in your browser, so nothing leaves your device.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF you want to split.
2. Choose every page as its own PDF, or type the page ranges you want.
3. Click Split PDF, then download the files or one ZIP.

Limits:
- The tool cannot split password-protected PDFs. Remove the password first.
- Extracted ranges keep their original page order. The tool does not reorder pages.
- Splitting every page of a long PDF depends on your device memory.

Q: How do I extract only certain pages?
A: Choose Extract page ranges and type the pages, separated by commas, such as 2, 4-6. You get one new PDF with only those pages.

Q: What happens when I split every page?
A: Each page becomes its own PDF, named after the original file plus the page number. With several files, you can download them together as a ZIP.

Q: Does splitting change my pages?
A: No. The tool copies the pages unchanged, so text stays selectable and images keep their quality.

Q: Can I split a password-protected PDF?
A: No. Remove the password in the app that created the file, then split it.

---

## Compress PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/compress-pdf
Compress PDF shrinks scanned and image-heavy PDFs by redrawing each page as an optimised image. The text in the compressed copy is no longer selectable, so the tool works best for scans and picture-based documents.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF you want to make smaller.
2. Pick Light, Recommended or Strong compression.
3. Click Compress PDF, then compare the sizes before and after.

Limits:
- The tool turns every page into an image, so you lose selectable text.
- The tool returns your original file when it cannot make a smaller one.
- The tool has no target-size setting. You pick a level and check the result.

Q: How much smaller will my PDF get?
A: It depends on the content. Scans and photo-heavy PDFs often shrink a lot. In our test, a PDF full of photos dropped by about 79 percent, while simple text PDFs may not shrink at all.

Q: What if my PDF is already small?
A: The tool returns your original file unchanged and tells you so, so you never get a bigger result.

Q: Can I still select text after compression?
A: No. The tool saves pages as images, so you cannot select or search the text. Keep the original, or run OCR PDF on the compressed copy.

Q: Which level should I choose?
A: Choose Light for the best quality, Recommended for a good balance, and Strong for the smallest file.

---

## OCR PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/ocr-pdf
OCR PDF reads the text in a scanned PDF and adds it as an invisible layer on top of your original pages. The PDF becomes searchable, you can select and copy its text, and the tool also gives you a .txt file. Everything runs in your browser.

How to use:
1. Add a scanned PDF.
2. Choose the language of the text and, if you want, the pages to read.
3. Click Make PDF searchable, then download the PDF and the text file.

Limits:
- English, Spanish, French and German give a searchable PDF. Urdu, Hindi and Arabic give a text file only.
- The tool reads up to 100 pages at a time.
- Handwriting, faint scans and tilted photos read poorly.

Q: What is the difference between OCR PDF and Image to Text?
A: Image to Text reads one picture and returns plain text. OCR PDF reads a whole PDF, keeps your pages exactly as they look, and adds the text underneath so the PDF itself becomes searchable.

Q: Does OCR PDF change how my PDF looks?
A: No. The tool keeps the original pages and adds the recognised text as an invisible layer. The pages look the same, but you can now search and copy text.

Q: Why do Urdu, Hindi and Arabic give only a text file?
A: The searchable layer needs a Latin-script font. The tool reads those languages and gives you the text, but it cannot place the text inside the PDF.

Q: What happens to pages that already have text?
A: The tool detects them and leaves them as they are, so it never reads a page twice.

---

## PDF to Word
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/pdf-to-word
PDF to Word extracts the text from a PDF and saves it as an editable .docx file. It keeps paragraphs and page breaks, but not the layout, fonts or images, and it needs a PDF with real text instead of a scan.

How to use:
1. Add a PDF that contains selectable text.
2. Click Convert to Word.
3. Download the .docx file and open it in Word, Google Docs or LibreOffice.

Limits:
- The tool drops images, tables, columns and fonts.
- The tool finds no text in scanned PDFs.
- Complex layouts, such as multi-column pages, need manual tidying afterwards.

Q: Will the layout and images stay?
A: No. This tool extracts text only. Tables, images, columns and fonts do not carry over, so expect to reformat the document.

Q: Why do I see a "no selectable text" message?
A: The PDF is probably a scan, which holds pictures of text. Run OCR PDF first to add a text layer, then convert the searchable PDF.

Q: Which file format does the tool create?
A: It creates a standard .docx file that opens in Microsoft Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice and Pages.

Q: Can I convert a PDF that has several columns?
A: Yes, but the tool reads the text line by line, so columns can mix. Tidy the result in your editor.

---

## PDF to JPG
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/pdf-to-jpg
PDF to JPG turns each page of a PDF into a JPG image. You can convert all pages or only chosen ones, pick the quality, and download the images one by one or as a ZIP. Everything runs in your browser.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF you want to convert.
2. Choose a quality (Small, Standard or High) and, if you want, the pages.
3. Click Convert to JPG, then download the images or the ZIP.

Limits:
- The tool makes one JPG per page, so a long PDF produces many files.
- Standard renders pages at 1.5 times their PDF size, High at 2 times and Small at 1 time.
- JPG compresses with some loss, so fine text can look soft on Small.

Q: What resolution do the images have?
A: Standard renders pages at 1.5 times their PDF size, High at 2 times and Small at 1 time. Higher settings give sharper but larger files.

Q: Can I convert a single page?
A: Yes. Type the page number, or a range such as 2-4, in the Pages box.

Q: Do I get one file or many?
A: You get one JPG per page. With several pages, you can download them all together as a ZIP.

Q: Should I choose JPG or PNG?
A: Choose JPG for pages with photos, because the files stay smaller. Choose PNG for text, line art and screenshots, because the edges stay sharp.

---

## JPG to PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/jpg-to-pdf
JPG to PDF combines one or more images into a single PDF, with one image per page. You can place each image on an A4 page or keep its own size, and you can reorder the pages before you create the file.

How to use:
1. Add your images (JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF or BMP).
2. Set the page order and choose A4 or same-size pages.
3. Click Create PDF, then download images.pdf.

Limits:
- The PDF holds your images as pictures, so the text inside photos stays unsearchable until you run OCR PDF.
- The tool converts non-JPG images to PNG inside the PDF to keep transparency and quality.
- Many large photos depend on your device memory.

Q: Which image formats can I use?
A: Use JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF or BMP. The tool converts non-JPG images to PNG inside the PDF, so transparency and quality stay intact.

Q: Can I put many images in one PDF?
A: Yes. Add as many as you like. Each image becomes its own page, in the order shown.

Q: Does the PDF reduce my image quality?
A: No. The tool embeds JPG images as they are, so their quality does not drop.

Q: Can I search the text in my photos?
A: Not at first. The PDF holds pictures, not text. Run OCR PDF on the result to make it searchable.

---

## Word to PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/word-to-pdf
Word to PDF converts the text of a .docx document into a simple A4 PDF. It does not keep images, tables, fonts or styling, so it suits plain text documents better than formatted reports.

How to use:
1. Add a .docx Word file.
2. Click Convert to PDF.
3. Download the PDF.

Limits:
- The tool keeps text and simple paragraph spacing only.
- The tool reads .docx files, not older .doc files.
- The tool supports Latin characters only and replaces all others with a question mark.

Q: Does it keep my formatting?
A: No. The tool converts only the text, with simple paragraph spacing. Images, tables, headers and fonts do not carry over.

Q: Can it convert old .doc files?
A: No. It reads only the modern .docx format. Open the old file in Word and save it as .docx first.

Q: What happens to non-English characters?
A: The PDF uses a standard Latin font, so characters outside it, such as Arabic, Urdu or Chinese, turn into question marks.

Q: Which page size does the PDF use?
A: The tool creates A4 pages and wraps the text to fit.

---

## PDF to PNG
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/pdf-to-png
PDF to PNG renders each page of a PDF as a lossless PNG image. You can choose all pages or a range, set the quality, and download the images one by one or as a ZIP. It runs entirely in your browser.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF you want to convert.
2. Choose a quality and, if you want, the pages to export.
3. Click Convert to PNG, then download the images.

Limits:
- PNG files stay large, because PNG keeps every detail.
- The tool makes one image per page.
- The images hold pictures of words, not text you can select.

Q: When should I choose PNG instead of JPG?
A: Choose PNG for text, line art and screenshots, because it stays sharp. Choose JPG for photographs, because the files stay smaller.

Q: Why are the PNG files large?
A: PNG keeps every detail and discards nothing. Use the Small quality setting, or switch to PDF to JPG, for smaller files.

Q: Can I export only some pages?
A: Yes. Enter pages such as 1-3, 5 in the Pages box.

Q: Do the images keep the PDF text?
A: No. Each image is a picture of the page. Use PDF to Text when you need the words.

---

## PDF to Excel
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/pdf-to-excel
PDF to Excel reads the text on each PDF page, groups it into rows and columns, and saves an .xlsx workbook with one sheet per page. It works best on clean text tables, not on scans or complex layouts.

How to use:
1. Add a PDF that contains selectable text.
2. Click Convert to Excel.
3. Download the .xlsx file and check the columns.

Limits:
- The tool guesses table structure from text positions, so merged cells and multi-column layouts need manual tidying.
- The tool finds no text in scanned PDFs.
- The tool makes one sheet per page. It does not join tables across pages.

Q: How accurate is the table detection?
A: The tool does a best-effort job based on text positions. Clean tables convert well. Merged cells, scans and multi-column layouts usually need manual tidying.

Q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
A: Not directly. Scans have no selectable text. Run OCR PDF first, then convert the searchable PDF.

Q: How does the tool arrange pages in the workbook?
A: Each PDF page becomes its own sheet, named Page 1, Page 2 and so on.

Q: Which Excel format does it create?
A: It creates an .xlsx workbook that opens in Excel, Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

---

## Excel to PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/excel-to-pdf
Excel to PDF draws each sheet of an .xlsx, .xls, .csv or .ods file as a table in a landscape PDF. It does not keep cell formatting or charts, and it supports Latin characters only.

How to use:
1. Add an Excel, CSV or ODS file.
2. Click Convert to PDF.
3. Download the PDF, which has one section per sheet.

Limits:
- The tool drops colours, charts and cell formatting.
- The tool scales wide sheets to the page width and shortens long cell text.
- The tool supports Latin characters only and replaces other scripts with a question mark.

Q: Does the PDF keep colours, charts and formulas?
A: No. The PDF shows the cell values as plain text in a table. Colours, charts and formatting do not carry over.

Q: What happens to wide sheets?
A: The tool scales the columns to fit the page width and shortens long cell text so the table stays on the page.

Q: Can it handle non-English text?
A: Only Latin characters work. The tool replaces other scripts with a question mark.

Q: How does the tool handle several sheets?
A: It adds one section to the PDF for each sheet.

---

## Rotate PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/rotate-pdf
Rotate PDF turns every page, or only the pages you choose, by 90 degrees clockwise, 90 degrees counter-clockwise or 180 degrees. The rest of the document stays unchanged, and the tool works in your browser.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF.
2. Choose the rotation and, if you want, the pages, such as 2-4.
3. Click Rotate PDF, then download the result.

Limits:
- The tool rotates by 90 degrees either way, or by 180 degrees.
- The tool cannot rotate password-protected PDFs.
- The tool changes orientation only. It does not straighten tilted scans.

Q: Can I rotate only one page?
A: Yes. Type the page number in the Pages box, and the tool rotates only that page.

Q: Is the rotation permanent?
A: Yes. The tool saves it into the new file, so every PDF viewer shows the pages the new way up.

Q: Will the text stay selectable?
A: Yes. The tool changes only the page orientation and does not redraw the content.

Q: Can I rotate by any angle?
A: No. Choose 90 degrees clockwise, 90 degrees counter-clockwise or 180 degrees.

---

## Watermark PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/watermark-pdf
Watermark PDF stamps your own text, such as CONFIDENTIAL or DRAFT, across every page of a PDF. You choose the opacity and whether the text runs diagonally or horizontally. It supports standard Latin characters.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF.
2. Type your watermark text and pick the opacity and angle.
3. Click Add watermark, then download the stamped PDF.

Limits:
- The tool adds text watermarks only. It cannot add a logo or image.
- The tool supports standard Latin letters, numbers and punctuation.
- The tool draws the text onto each page, so it does not protect the file from copying.

Q: Can I choose the watermark text?
A: Yes. Type any text with standard Latin letters, numbers and punctuation.

Q: Can someone remove the watermark afterwards?
A: The tool draws the text onto each page and gives no real protection. Keep your original file and share only the stamped copy.

Q: Can I use a logo or an image?
A: Not yet. This tool adds text watermarks only.

Q: Does the watermark change my original file?
A: No. The tool creates a new stamped PDF and leaves your original untouched.

---

## PDF to Text
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/pdf-to-text
PDF to Text pulls the selectable text out of a PDF, page by page, and gives you a plain .txt file. It works on PDFs with real text, while scanned PDFs need OCR PDF first.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF.
2. Click Extract text.
3. Copy the text from the box, or download the .txt file.

Limits:
- The tool finds no text in scanned PDFs.
- The tool reads each page top to bottom and left to right, so columns can mix.
- The tool drops images and layout. You get plain text only.

Q: Why is the result empty?
A: The PDF is probably a scan made of images. Run OCR PDF to add a text layer, then extract the text from the searchable PDF.

Q: Does the tool keep the line order?
A: The tool reads each page top to bottom and left to right, with a blank line between pages. Columns and tables may need tidying.

Q: Can I copy the text without downloading?
A: Yes. The extracted text appears in a box with a Copy text button.

Q: Does the text keep its formatting?
A: No. You get plain text. Bold, fonts, images and layout do not carry over.

---

## Sign PDF
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/sign-pdf
Sign PDF lets you draw your signature and place it on the first, last or every page of a PDF. You choose the position and size. The tool adds a visual signature image, not a certificate-based digital signature.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF you want to sign.
2. Draw your signature, then choose the page, position and size.
3. Click Sign PDF, then download the signed copy.

Limits:
- The tool adds an image of your signature. It does not add a certificate-based digital signature.
- The tool offers four positions and three page choices: first, last or all pages.
- The tool cannot sign password-protected PDFs.

Q: Is this a legally binding digital signature?
A: It is a visual signature image placed on the page. It uses no certificate, so check that the person or authority you sign for accepts it.

Q: Can I sign on my phone?
A: Yes. Draw with your finger in the signature box.

Q: Can I place the signature anywhere?
A: You can choose bottom right, bottom left, bottom centre or centre, on the first, last or all pages.

Q: Where does my signature go?
A: Nowhere outside your device. You draw it in your browser, and the tool places it on your PDF locally.

---

## PDF to PPT
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/pdf-to-ppt
PDF to PPT converts each page of a PDF into a slide in a .pptx file. The slides hold page images, so they look exactly like the PDF, but you cannot edit the text on them.

How to use:
1. Add the PDF.
2. Click Convert to PowerPoint.
3. Download the .pptx file and open it in PowerPoint, Keynote or Google Slides.

Limits:
- The tool cannot edit slide text, because each slide holds an image.
- The tool sizes the slides to the first PDF page.
- Long PDFs create large .pptx files.

Q: Can I edit the text on the slides?
A: No. Each slide holds an image of the PDF page, so you cannot edit text or shapes.

Q: What slide size does the tool use?
A: The slides take the proportions of the first PDF page.

Q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
A: Yes. The tool uses pages as images, so scans convert fine.

Q: Which presentation programs open the file?
A: PowerPoint, Keynote and Google Slides open the .pptx file.

---

## Compress Image
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/compress-image
The image compressor reduces the file size of JPG, PNG and WebP images in your browser, so your photos never leave your device. Pick a compression level or type a target size such as 100 KB, add as many images as you like, and download the smaller files.

How to use:
1. Drop your images in, or click Choose images. You can add many at once.
2. Pick Light, Balanced, Strong or Maximum, or type a target size in KB.
3. Download each image, or click Download all.

Limits:
- PNG is lossless, so the quality slider does not change PNG files. Resize, or switch to WebP or JPG.
- With a target size, the tool saves PNG images as JPG and fills transparent areas with white.
- The tool marks a file as Over target when it cannot reach your limit.

Q: How much smaller will my images get?
A: Typical photos shrink by 40 to 80 percent at Balanced quality with little visible change. Images that are already well compressed shrink less.

Q: How do I compress an image to 100 KB, 50 KB or 20 KB?
A: Type the size in the Target size box, or tap the 20, 50, 100 or 200 KB button. The tool finds the highest quality that fits and reduces the pixel size only when it must.

Q: Is PNG compression lossless?
A: Yes. PNG is lossless, so the quality slider does not change it. To shrink a PNG, resize it, or convert it to WebP or JPG.

Q: What if the result is bigger than the original?
A: When the format and size stay the same and the new file would grow, the tool keeps your original and marks it Already optimal.

---

## Resize Image
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/resize-image
Resize Image changes the width and height of a picture to the exact pixel size you enter. It runs in your browser, so your image stays on your device, and you can download the resized file straight away.

How to use:
1. Add an image.
2. Enter the width and height in pixels.
3. Click Resize Image, then download the result.

Limits:
- The tool saves the result as a JPG.
- The tool fills transparent areas with white.
- The tool cannot add detail when you enlarge a picture.

Q: Does it keep the aspect ratio?
A: Turn on Keep proportions and enter one side. The tool calculates the other side for you. Turn it off to stretch the image to exact dimensions.

Q: Which formats can I resize?
A: You can resize JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP images. The tool saves the result as a JPG.

Q: Will resizing reduce the file size?
A: Usually yes, because fewer pixels need less data. For more control, use the Image Compressor.

Q: Can I resize many images at once?
A: Not yet. Resize one image at a time, or set a Max width in the Image Compressor to shrink a batch.

---

## Convert to JPG
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/convert-to-jpg
Convert to JPG changes PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP images into the widely supported JPG format. The tool fills transparent areas with white, because JPG does not support transparency.

How to use:
1. Add an image.
2. Click Convert to JPG.
3. Download the JPG file.

Limits:
- The tool saves JPG at high quality (92 percent), which still loses a little detail.
- The tool fills transparency with white.
- The tool converts one image at a time.

Q: What happens to transparency?
A: JPG cannot store transparency, so the tool fills transparent areas with white.

Q: Will the quality drop?
A: JPG is a lossy format, so you lose a small amount of detail. The tool saves the file at high quality (92 percent).

Q: Can I convert many images at once?
A: Not yet. Convert one image at a time, or use the Image Compressor for batches.

Q: Which formats can I convert?
A: You can convert PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP images.

---

## Convert to PNG
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/convert-to-png
Convert to PNG saves JPG, WebP, GIF and BMP images as lossless PNG files. PNG keeps sharp edges and transparency, which suits graphics, screenshots and logos. It runs in your browser.

How to use:
1. Add an image.
2. Click Convert to PNG.
3. Download the PNG file.

Limits:
- The tool cannot restore detail that a JPG already lost.
- The tool makes larger files than JPG for photos.
- The tool keeps transparency only when the source image has it.

Q: Does converting JPG to PNG improve quality?
A: No. PNG cannot restore detail that the JPG already removed. It only stops further loss when you edit and save again.

Q: Why is the PNG bigger than the JPG?
A: PNG stores every pixel without discarding detail, so photographs make larger files.

Q: Does the tool keep transparency?
A: Yes, when the source image has it, for example a WebP or GIF.

Q: Which formats can I convert?
A: You can convert JPG, WebP, GIF and BMP images.

---

## Convert to WebP
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/convert-to-webp
Convert to WebP changes JPG, PNG, GIF and BMP images into WebP, a modern format that is usually smaller than JPG or PNG at similar quality. All current browsers support it.

How to use:
1. Add an image.
2. Click Convert to WebP.
3. Download the WebP file.

Limits:
- Some older software and apps cannot open WebP files.
- The saving varies by picture, so WebP is not always smaller.
- The tool keeps your original file and creates a new WebP copy.

Q: Why use WebP?
A: WebP files are typically smaller than equivalent JPG or PNG files, which makes web pages load faster.

Q: Does every program support WebP?
A: All current browsers support it. Some older software and apps cannot open WebP files.

Q: Does WebP support transparency?
A: Yes. WebP supports transparency, like PNG.

Q: How much smaller is WebP?
A: Google reports that lossy WebP files are 25 to 34 percent smaller than comparable JPEGs. Your saving depends on the picture.

---

## Crop Image
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/crop-image
Crop Image lets you drag a selection box over your picture. Choose a free or fixed shape, such as 1:1, 4:3 or 16:9, and download the cropped result as PNG, JPG or WebP. It runs in your browser.

How to use:
1. Add an image.
2. Choose a shape, then drag the box and its corners to frame the part you want.
3. Click Crop image, then download the result.

Limits:
- The tool offers free, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9 and 3:4 shapes.
- The tool crops rectangular areas only, not freehand shapes.
- The tool saves PNG, JPG or WebP.

Q: Can I crop to a square or 16:9?
A: Yes. Pick 1:1, 4:3, 16:9 or 3:4, and the box keeps that ratio while you resize it.

Q: What quality does the cropped image have?
A: The tool cuts from the original full-size image, not the preview, so you lose no resolution.

Q: Which formats can I save as?
A: You can save as PNG, JPG or WebP.

Q: Which formats can I crop?
A: You can crop JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP images.

---

## Rotate and Flip Image
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/rotate-flip-image
Rotate and Flip Image turns a picture 90 degrees left or right, or 180 degrees, and optionally mirrors it horizontally or vertically. It runs in your browser and saves the result as a JPG.

How to use:
1. Add an image.
2. Choose the rotation and, if you need it, a flip direction.
3. Click Rotate and Flip Image, then download the result.

Limits:
- The tool rotates by 90 degrees left, 90 degrees right or 180 degrees only.
- The tool re-saves the image as a high-quality JPG, so you lose a tiny amount of detail.
- The tool fills transparency with white.

Q: Can I flip without rotating?
A: Choose a flip direction and rotate by 180 or 90 degrees as needed. Combining them covers every orientation.

Q: Does the tool lose quality?
A: The tool re-saves the file as a high-quality JPG, so you lose a small amount of detail.

Q: Can I rotate by any angle?
A: Not yet. You can rotate by 90 degrees left, 90 degrees right or 180 degrees.

Q: Which formats can I use?
A: You can use JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP images.

---

## Grayscale Image
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/grayscale-image
Grayscale Image converts a colour picture to black and white with standard luminance weights. It runs in your browser, so your photo stays on your device, and it saves the result as a JPG.

How to use:
1. Add a colour image.
2. Click Grayscale Image.
3. Download the black and white image.

Limits:
- The tool cannot restore the colours.
- The tool saves the result as a JPG file.
- The tool uses fixed luminance weights, with no manual contrast control.

Q: How does the tool calculate the grey level?
A: Each pixel uses the common luminance formula (29.9 percent red, 58.7 percent green and 11.4 percent blue), which matches how the eye sees brightness.

Q: Can I get the colours back?
A: No. Keep your original image if you may need the colour version.

Q: Which format does the tool save?
A: It saves a high-quality JPG.

Q: Can I adjust the contrast?
A: Not yet. The tool uses fixed luminance weights.

---

## Watermark Image
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/watermark-image
Watermark Image writes your own text diagonally across a picture, with adjustable opacity. It runs in your browser, so your photo stays on your device, and the tool saves the result as a JPG.

How to use:
1. Add an image.
2. Type your watermark text and choose the opacity.
3. Click Watermark Image, then download the result.

Limits:
- The tool adds text watermarks only. It cannot add a logo.
- The tool centres the text across the image at a slight angle.
- The tool saves the result as a JPG file.

Q: Can I use my own text?
A: Yes. Type any text, such as your name or website, and choose how visible it is.

Q: Where does the watermark sit?
A: The tool centres it across the image at a slight angle.

Q: Can I add a logo?
A: Not yet. This tool adds text watermarks only.

Q: Does the watermark change my original?
A: No. The tool saves a new file and leaves your original untouched.

## Upscale Image
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/upscale-image
Upscale Image makes a picture 2, 3 or 4 times larger with smooth resampling and optional sharpening. It enlarges cleanly, but it does not invent new detail the way AI upscalers do.

How to use:
1. Add an image.
2. Choose the scale, the sharpening level and the output format.
3. Click Upscale image, then download the larger version.

Limits:
- The tool does not add missing detail, because it is not an AI upscaler.
- The tool refuses results above about 9,000 pixels on a side or 64 megapixels.
- PNG keeps every detail but makes big files.

Q: Is this AI upscaling?
A: No. The tool uses high-quality resampling and sharpening. The results look cleaner than simple stretching, but they do not add missing detail.

Q: What is the maximum size?
A: The tool refuses results larger than about 9,000 pixels on a side or 64 megapixels, to protect your device.

Q: Which output format is best?
A: PNG keeps every detail but makes big files. JPG and WebP make smaller files.

Q: Which scale should I choose?
A: Try 2x first. Higher scales enlarge every flaw in the picture.

## Image to Text
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/image-to-text
Image to Text uses optical character recognition (OCR) to read the text in a photo or screenshot and return it as editable text. It runs in your browser, so the picture stays on your device.

How to use:
1. Add an image or screenshot that contains text.
2. Choose the language of the text.
3. Click Extract text, then copy the result or download the .txt file.

Limits:
- The tool reads English, Urdu, Hindi, Arabic, Spanish, French and German.
- The tool reads one image at a time. For a whole scanned PDF, use OCR PDF.
- Blurry pictures and handwriting read poorly.

Q: Which languages does the tool support?
A: It supports English, Urdu, Hindi, Arabic, Spanish, French and German.

Q: Why does the first run take longer?
A: Your browser downloads the recognition data for the language the first time. After that, the tool runs faster.

Q: How can I get better results?
A: Use a sharp, high-resolution picture with dark text on a plain background and straight lines of text.

Q: Can it read a whole PDF?
A: Not here. Use OCR PDF to read a scanned PDF and keep the pages as they look.

## Compress Video
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/compress-video
Compress Video makes a video file smaller by re-encoding it with H.264 and AAC, with a choice of quality and maximum resolution. It runs on your own device, so the video never leaves it.

How to use:
1. Add a video (MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, AVI and more).
2. Pick the compression level and, if you want, a maximum resolution.
3. Click Compress video, then download the smaller MP4.

Limits:
- The tool refuses files over about 700 MB, because browsers have limited memory.
- The first run downloads a video engine of about 30 MB.
- The tool returns your original when it cannot make a smaller file.

Q: How long does it take?
A: It runs on your device, so the time depends on the video length and your computer. Short clips take seconds, and long high-resolution videos take several minutes.

Q: Is there a size limit?
A: Yes. The tool refuses files over about 700 MB, because browsers have limited memory.

Q: What if my video is already small?
A: The tool returns your original unchanged and says so.

Q: Why does the tool download 30 MB first?
A: It downloads a video engine the first time you use a video tool. Your browser keeps it for next time.

## Trim Video
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/trim-video
Trim Video cuts a video to the start and end times you set. Fast mode copies the video without re-encoding, which works quickly but cuts at the nearest keyframe. Exact mode re-encodes the clip for frame-accurate cuts.

How to use:
1. Add a video.
2. Type the start and end time, such as 0:05 and 0:30, and choose Fast or Exact.
3. Click Trim video, then download the clip.

Limits:
- Fast mode can cut a moment early or late, because it cuts at keyframes.
- The tool refuses files over about 700 MB.
- Exact mode takes longer, because it re-encodes the clip.

Q: What is the difference between Fast and Exact?
A: Fast copies the existing video data, so it works quickly with no quality loss, but the cut can sit a moment off. Exact re-encodes the clip, so the cut lands precisely.

Q: Which time formats can I use?
A: Use seconds (90), minutes and seconds (1:30), or hours, minutes and seconds (0:01:30).

Q: Can I leave the end time blank?
A: Yes. The clip then runs from your start time to the end of the video.

Q: Which formats can I trim?
A: You can trim MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM and AVI files.

## Convert Video
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/convert-video
Convert Video changes a video file into MP4, WebM, MOV, MKV or AVI. The conversion runs in your browser, so the file stays on your device, and MP4 (H.264 and AAC) plays on nearly every device.

How to use:
1. Add a video.
2. Choose the format to convert to.
3. Click Convert video, then download the file.

Limits:
- The tool re-encodes the video at good quality (H.264 CRF 23 for MP4, MOV and MKV), so a small loss is possible.
- The tool refuses files over about 700 MB.
- The tool aims for quality, not for a file size.

Q: Which format should I pick?
A: MP4 works almost everywhere. WebM suits websites, MOV suits Apple software, and MKV and AVI suit specific players.

Q: Will the quality change?
A: The tool re-encodes the video at good quality (H.264 CRF 23 for MP4, MOV and MKV), so you may lose a little detail.

Q: Why is conversion slow?
A: It runs on your device, so long or high-resolution videos take longer.

Q: Can I convert a video to MP3?
A: Not here. Use Extract Audio from Video to save the sound as MP3, M4A or WAV.

Q: Is there a limit on clips?
A: The tool sets no fixed limit, but the total size must stay under about 700 MB.

URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/gif-to-video
GIF to Video turns an animated GIF into an MP4 video. The MP4 is usually much smaller than the GIF and plays smoothly on phones and websites. The conversion runs in your browser.

How to use:
1. Add a GIF.
2. Click Convert to MP4.
3. Download the MP4.

Limits:
- The tool accepts GIF files only.
- The MP4 does not loop by itself. Your player or embed controls looping.
- Colours can shift slightly after the conversion.

Q: Why convert a GIF to MP4?
A: MP4 files are usually many times smaller than the same animation as a GIF, and they play more smoothly.

Q: Does the MP4 loop?

A: Slightly. MP4 uses a different colour format, but the results look close.

Q: Can I turn the MP4 back into a GIF?

## JSON Formatter
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/json-formatter
JSON Formatter checks that your JSON is valid and rewrites it with clean indentation, so it is easy to read. When something is wrong, it shows the error message from the parser.

How to use:
1. Paste your JSON into the input box.
2. Read the formatted result on the right, with a valid or error message.
3. Click Copy JSON to copy the result.

Limits:
- The tool checks syntax only. It does not check a schema.
- The tool indents with two spaces and has no other setting.
- Large inputs depend on your device memory.

Q: Does it validate JSON?
A: Yes. It shows Valid JSON, or the error message from the parser.

Q: Does the tool send my data anywhere?
A: No. Formatting happens in your browser.

Q: How does the tool indent the output?
A: It uses two spaces per level.

Q: Why does my JSON show an error?
A: Common causes are a trailing comma, single quotes instead of double quotes, and keys without quotes. The error message shows what the parser found.

## Base64 Encoder and Decoder
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/base64-encoder-decoder
The Base64 Encoder and Decoder converts text to Base64 and decodes Base64 back to readable text, including characters outside basic English (UTF-8). It runs in your browser, so your text stays on your device.

How to use:
1. Choose Encode or Decode.
2. Type or paste your text.
3. Click Copy Result.

Limits:
- The tool encodes text, not files.
- Base64 hides nothing, because anyone can decode it.
- The tool treats text as UTF-8.

Q: What is Base64?
A: Base64 represents data with only letters, digits, plus and slash, so it can travel safely through systems that handle only text.

Q: Is Base64 encryption?
A: No. Anyone can decode it, so never use it to protect secrets.

Q: Does it support emoji and other languages?
A: Yes. The tool handles text as UTF-8.

Q: Does the encoded text get longer?
A: Yes. Base64 output is about one third larger than the original.

## URL Encoder and Decoder
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/url-encoder-decoder
The URL Encoder and Decoder converts text into percent-encoded form that is safe to use in a web address, and decodes it back. For example, a space becomes %20 and an ampersand becomes %26.

How to use:
1. Choose Encode or Decode.
2. Type or paste your text.
3. Click Copy Result.

Limits:
- The tool encodes every character except letters, digits and a few safe symbols.
- The tool shows Invalid input when it cannot decode a string.
- The tool encodes a whole URL as one piece, including its slashes.

Q: Which characters does the tool encode?
A: It encodes everything except letters, digits and a few safe symbols, with the standard encodeURIComponent rules.

Q: What does decode do with invalid input?
A: It shows Invalid input instead of guessing.

Q: Should I encode a whole URL?
A: Encode only the parts you add, such as query values. Encoding a full URL also encodes its slashes and colons.

Q: Does it work with non-English text?
A: Yes. The tool encodes any text as UTF-8.

## Hash Generator
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/hash-generator
Hash Generator creates SHA-256, SHA-1 and SHA-512 hashes of any text with the cryptography that your browser provides. The tool never sends your text to a server, so your input stays private.

How to use:
1. Type or paste your text.
2. Read the three hashes as they appear.
3. Copy the one you need.

Limits:
- The tool hashes text only. It does not hash files.
- The tool does not offer MD5.
- The tool offers SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 only.

Q: Does the tool include MD5?
A: No. The browser does not provide MD5, and MD5 is not secure. SHA-256 is the recommended choice.

Q: Can someone reverse a hash?
A: No. Hashes work one way, though attackers can look up weak hashes of common words.

Q: Can I hash a file?
A: Not yet. This tool hashes text only.

Q: Why does one extra space change the hash?
A: A hash covers every character, so even a space or a new line produces a completely different result.

## Case Converter
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/case-converter

- The tool works on the text in the box, one block at a time.

Q: What is the difference between camelCase and PascalCase?
A: camelCase starts with a lowercase letter (myVariableName). PascalCase starts with a capital (MyVariableName).

Q: What is snake_case?
A: snake_case writes words in lowercase and joins them with underscores, for example my_variable_name.

Q: Does Title Case follow style guides?
A: It capitalises the first letter of every word. It does not skip small words such as of or the.

Q: Which case suits a URL slug?
A: kebab-case suits URL slugs, because it joins lowercase words with hyphens.

---

## Text Reverser
URL: https://www.tinywownow.com/text-reverser
Text Reverser flips your text by characters, by words or by lines. Type or paste text, and the reversed version appears instantly. It runs in your browser, so your text stays private.

How to use:
1. Type or paste your text.
2. Choose Reverse Characters, Reverse Words or Reverse Lines.
3. Click Copy Result.

Limits:
- The tool reverses by characters, words or lines only.
- Reversing characters can split multi-part emoji.
- The tool works on one block of text at a time.

Q: What is the difference between the three modes?
A: Characters reverses every letter ("abc" becomes "cba"). Words reverses the order of the words. Lines reverses the order of the lines.

Q: Does it work with emoji?
A: Basic emoji work, but reversing characters can split some multi-part emoji.

Q: Does the tool save my text?
A: No. Your text stays in your browser.

Q: Can I reverse a list?
A: Yes. Paste the list, one item per line, and choose Reverse Lines.
